findings.suggested_fix: Include open details identifiers or stable indices in each entry snapshot, capture toggle events, and apply that state immediately after render() and before focus/scroll restoration. Verify expanded bass and sample disclosures across Back/Forward at desktop and narrow widths.
findings.title: Restore disclosure state before scroll
findings.why_it_matters: Returning to an expanded musical task closes its disclosure and can jump the reader to a different position. Re-rendering discards open details before the saved scroll is applied, so the shorter page clamps the requested position; the scroll listener then overwrites the history entry with that wrong position. Preserve each entry’s open disclosures and restore them before measuring or scrolling.

docs/website-v4-corrections-20261114/site/navigation.js:29 --    focus?.focus({preventScroll:true});scrollTo(0,saved?.y||0);restoringRoute=false;

Independent Chromium reproduction at 1440x900: open #learn/bass directly, expand Let the phrase drift, scroll the next-task link into view. Before leaving, scrollY=471, document max scroll=471, details.open=true. Follow next-task link and Back: details.open=false, max scroll=294, scrollY=294; history entry is overwritten with y=294.

Reproduced against http://127.0.0.1:4321/#learn/bass with Playwright Chromium: open details; scroll footer Home into view; before={y:1057,height:1757,open:true}; click footer Home; browser Back; after={y:817,height:1517,open:false}. The saved entry is then overwritten with the clamped y=817 by the subsequent scroll snapshot.

findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish popstate for a newly created fragment entry without dnboxRoute state from a saved traversal. Initialize the entry and use navigate mode so the heading receives focus; test address-bar and location.hash navigation plus subsequent Back/Forward.
findings.title: Initialize entries for direct hash navigation
findings.why_it_matters: A newly assigned fragment route can render without focusing its heading and without receiving history state. Chromium fires popstate with null state before hashchange for location.hash navigation; the popstate handler uses history mode and marks renderedURL current, so the later hashchange returns without initializing the entry. The page keeps the prior focused navigation element and cannot record its new reading position.
evidence: docs/website-v4-corrections-20261114/site/navigation.js:50 -- window.addEventListener('popstate',()=>showRoute('history'));
docs/website-v4-corrections-20261114/site/navigation.js:53 --  if(renderedURL===location.href)return;
Independent Chromium seam: focused skip anchor, then location.hash=learn/bass; route renders with A focus and history.state=null. See independent-browser-seams.json.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a focusin listener that snapshots the current entry outside restoration, using the existing rememberRoutePosition helper; ensure focused controls and route headings receive stable restoration locators, then test focus-only changes followed by Back/Forward.
findings.title: Persist focus before browser history traversal
findings.why_it_matters: Keyboard users lose their place when they focus a control and then use browser Back and Forward without scrolling. The entry is saved only on link clicks, scroll and pagehide; same-document history traversal emits no pagehide, so the focused control never enters the saved state and Forward returns focus to BODY. Persist focus changes as they occur, while suppressing restoration-generated snapshots.
evidence: docs/website-v4-corrections-20261114/site/navigation.js:50 -- window.addEventListener('popstate',()=>showRoute('history'));
docs/website-v4-corrections-20261114/site/navigation.js:49 -- window.addEventListener('pagehide',rememberRoutePosition);

Independent Chromium reproduction at 1440x900: #home -> nav Guide -> #learn/beat; focus #teacher-next while scrollY=0. Before Back, history.state.dnboxRoute={y:0,focus:null}. Back then Forward restores #learn/beat with document.activeElement.tagName=BODY, id empty, scrollY=0.
docs/website-v4-corrections-20261114/site/navigation.js:47 --  scrollSnapshotPending=true;requestAnimationFrame(()=>{scrollSnapshotPending=false;if(!restoringRoute)rememberRoutePosition();});

Reproduced with real Playwright keyboard input at 1440×900: open #home, click header Guide, press Shift+Tab four times -> activeElement href #files, y=0, history focus null. Browser Back then Forward -> activeElement href #learn, y=0, history focus remains null. Same-document traversal does not dispatch pagehide.
site/navigation.js:50 -- window.addEventListener('popstate',()=>showRoute('history'));
site/navigation.js:42 snapshots focus only for intercepted route-link clicks; lines 45-49 otherwise update on scroll and pagehide, with no focusin handler.
tests/navigation.py:11 records document.activeElement.outerHTML on Back but asserts only scroll position; line 12 likewise asserts Forward scroll only.

docs/website-v4-corrections-20261114/site/navigation.js:42 --  event.preventDefault();rememberRoutePosition();
